Crispy deep-fried eel, complemented by vermicelli and veg
Dec 2018 • Family
If it weren’t for the HanoiKids, we would not have found ourselves in this authentic eating spot, contentedly crunching crispy deep-fried eel, slurping slippery vermicelli and savouring sweet herbs/leaves that are piled generously on top of the serving of “Mien Luon”. Even if you don’t speak a word of Vietnamese, you’ll manage, as there’s a menu on the wall with large and clear illustrations of the dishes. Just point! We tried three variations, namely “Mien Xao” (fried vermicelli with egg), “Mien Muoc” (vermicelli soup) and “Mien Tron” (vermicelli blend)… the third one being my favourite, as eel takes center stage, nicely complemented by vermicelli and veg. Just had to add one more new Vietnamese word to my vocab, after our appetizing lunch here – “Ngon” (yummy)!

Very memorable
May 2017 • Family
My family of four ate here as part of a self designed morning food tour of the Old Quarter. This place came up several times on lists of places one must try in Hanoi. I have no idea how long it has been here, but probably for a while. I believe it is described in eloquent detail in chapter 5 of Graham Holliday's Eating Viet Nam book. It is a street food experience, not a restaurant really. Before you walk in, have a look at the glass case of eels. Watch the man frying the noodles. Then as you walk into the narrow seating area, look to your left - you will see six choices on the menu with pictures. Decide then what you want. You will sit down, then you will be approached by a waitress who probably speaks only Vietnamese. The waitress may seem impatient, but I suspect it is a combination of usually dealing with locals and the language barrier. If she seems abrupt, don't let it hurt your feelings. We tried both the broth based soup and the mien xao. Xao means fried in Vietnamese. This will be a stir fried glass noodle dish with the crispy fried eels, garnished with herbs, peanuts and fried shallots - it was my favorite, very tasty and unique. I think the eel may lose some of its crunchiness if submerged. Squeeze a bit of the 'decapitated' citrus fruit on your eel noodles and enjoy something you've never had. I think you will like this place if you are a foody with an adventurous spirit. These dishes are somewhat filling, so if you're on a street food odyssey, then share a bowl with a friend.
